# C12 — Poor Hardware Locality Usage

*Level 1 card. 4 root causes. Open the level-2 card before accepting any of them.*

Energy waste driven by CPU and memory hierarchy behavior such as cache misses, branch misprediction, and suboptimal memory access patterns. While Python developers have limited direct control over hardware-level behavior compared to C/C++, certain access patterns (especially when using NumPy, array.array, or ctypes for numerical work) can still trigger cache inefficiencies. This category covers patterns where restructuring data access order or layout can improve cache utilization, reduce memory-bus traffic, and lower branch misprediction penalties.

## Root causes in this category

| ID | Name | Looks for | The repair | Measurable? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **C12.S1** | Inefficient Large-Stride Traversal | a contiguous buffer traversed against the direction its memory is laid out in | traverse along the contiguous axis, or store the array in the layout the traversal needs | yes, scales with input |
| **C12.S2** | Sparse Element Access | scattered reads into a large buffer, using one element of every cache line fetched | sort or group the accesses so nearby indices are visited together | yes, scales with input |
| **C12.S3** | Unpredictable Branches | a data-dependent branch in a compiled hot loop that the CPU cannot predict | make the branch predictable, or replace it with branchless arithmetic | yes, scales with input |
| **C12.S4** | Inefficient Array Declaration Order | a declared struct whose field order puts cold data in front of hot data | declare the hot fields first | **no — advisory only** |

Card paths: `reference/root-causes/C12.S1.md`, `reference/root-causes/C12.S2.md`, `reference/root-causes/C12.S3.md`, `reference/root-causes/C12.S4.md`

## If nothing here fits

Say so and move on. Reporting a weak match from a category you have already opened is the most common way this analysis goes wrong: the category is open because something drew you here, which is not the same as a smell being present.
